models_evaluated: API versions and May 2026 free-tier versions of the same three models

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM responses across repeated identical queries in independent sessions
links.effect: Reproducible responses: model C 92.0%, model A 72.0% (P=0.028 vs C), model B 68.0% (P=0.008 vs C); non-reproducible answers in 8-32% of questions.
links.quote: For consistency, model C demonstrated a significantly higher rate of reproducible responses (92.0%) compared with model A (72.0%, P = 0.028) and model B (68.0%, P = 0.008).

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with the 2022 ESHRE endometriosis guideline (reliability)
links.effect: Reliability 76.0% model C, 68.0% model A, 68.0% model B (no significant difference, P=0.598); none reached reliability required for unsupervised clinical use.
links.quote: No significant between-model differences were found for reliability (χ2 = 1.029, P = 0.598), with rates of 76.0% for model C, 68.0% for model A, and 68.0% for model B.

links.outcome: LLM answer accuracy (Global Quality Score) against guideline-based expert rating
links.effect: Median GQS: model A 5 (IQR 4-5), model C 4 (3-5), model B 3 (3-4); Kruskal-Wallis H=37.10, P<0.001; converged to 4 on API/May 2026 free tier.
links.quote: Model A achieved the highest median GQS (5, interquartile range [IQR] 4-5), followed by model C (4, IQR 3-5) and model B (3, IQR 3-4).

unlisted_practices: Comparing LLM output quality across free-tier versus API access
Repeated-query reproducibility testing of LLM answers

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the baseline accuracy, consistency, and guideline concordance of three large language models on questions derived from the ESHRE endometriosis guideline, comparing free-tier vs. API access. It does not evaluate a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
